_comment: Combat resolver tuning (docs/plan_predators.md). Severity constants the placeholder resolver reads; NOT creature identity (that lives on fauna_config/creatures). Playtest dials.
_comment_hit_chance: P(one unit's attack lands) - where the resolver's variance lives (docs/plan_hunt_through_combat.md 4.7). Drawn PER UNIT, so it is BINOMIAL IN FORCE SIZE: three hunters are a gamble, thirty are reliable. It never softens THE GATE - a unit below its target's defense deals max(0, a-d) = 0 per landed strike, so no number of successful rolls produces damage. Ships 1.0, which is an EXACT IDENTITY (no draw made, no randomness consumed), so THE FIGHT'S OWN STAGE is deterministic and forecast == actual is an exact identity for it. IT DOES NOT MAKE THE PRE-COMMIT RANGE A POINT, and an earlier draft of this line said it did: the RETREAT is a second, independent stage (fauna_config's per-species combat.wariness, authored 0.10-0.85 across the roster), it draws whatever this dial says, and its binomial is what gives every wild-hunt and raid row a real reported band today. Authoring a sub-1 chance here adds the fight's variance ON TOP of that, it does not switch the range on. The two stages are salted apart (fauna::FIGHT_SEED_SALT) so they compose as independent binomials rather than replaying one uniform against two thresholds.
_comment_wound_recovery_rate: Share of its own durability a wounded body knits back per turn OUT OF CONTACT - the decay half of the cross-turn damage ledger (docs/plan_hunt_through_combat.md 4.2). Linear in durability, so a ledger empties in exactly ceil(1/rate) idle turns whatever it held; a geometric decay of the bank would never reach zero. Applies only on turns with no contact - healing every turn regardless would make (hunters x effective_attack > rate x durability) a SECOND absolute threshold, which is the shape the accumulator exists to remove. Ships 0.2: five quiet turns and the animal is whole.
_comment_forecast_range_sigmas: How WIDE the pre-commit forecast's reported range is, in standard deviations of the take's own binomials (docs/plan_hunt_through_combat.md 6.4). A forecast has no event seed - retreat_seed is composed from (map_seed, tick, herd, party) and a projection cannot know a future tick - so it makes NO draw and reads the distribution instead: the point estimate is the mean and the reported low/high are this many sigmas either side. Ships 2.0, ~95% of a normal-approximated binomial, which is the '6-11, likely 9' the design asks for. It is a READOUT width, never a model term: nothing the sim resolves reads it. THE BAND IT SETS IS REAL ON EVERY WILD-HUNT AND RAID ROW - the roster authors combat.wariness at 0.10-0.85, so the retreat stage draws and its binomial has spread, and this lever is what decides how wide the reported low/high sit around it. (An earlier draft of this line ended 'at the shipped wariness 0 / hit_chance 1.0 the distribution is degenerate', which was true only before those values were authored.) Where NO stage draws the range still collapses to a point on its own, with no flag: the plant web, a pen, and a species a test holds at wariness 0. hit_chance 1.0 makes the FIGHT'S stage degenerate, not the whole distribution.
_comment_hunt_injury_damage_per_animal: Damage a hunt does to its own party per ANIMAL ENGAGED, independent of what the quarry swings (docs/plan_hunt_through_combat.md 4.6). Hunters fall, break bones, are trampled in a drive, cut themselves butchering - a harmless animal is not a risk-free day out. It scales with the ENGAGEMENT, not the quarry (more animals worked, more chances to get hurt), which is why it is one lever here and not a per-species field: the danger is in the activity, not in the rabbit. Rides the expedition_danger_multiplier like every other blow. Ships 0.15 - against a person's durability 20 that is a body down per ~133 animal-contacts, texture rather than a second combat model.
